note: Every row published on the site comes from this file. status: verified = confirmed on an official page or statute during this session; partially verified = applicability confirmed but a figure is not confirmed on the fetched page (flagged); user-provided = supplied by the owner, not confirmable from an official record (flagged); secondary = only from non-official sources (flagged, not used as a value).

rows.label: Federal estate & gift basic exclusion amount, 2026 deaths
rows.notes: Per person; with portability of the deceased spouse's unused exclusion a couple can combine to $30,000,000 in 2026 (CRS R48183). Annual gifts up to $19,000 per donee (2026) do not use it.

rows.label: Federal estate filing threshold, 2025 deaths
rows.notes: Shows the step-up in the exclusion after 2025.

rows.label: Annual gift tax exclusion, 2026
Top federal estate tax rate above the exclusion
rows.value: 40% of the taxable estate above the exclusion
rows.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-06: FTB analysis ('The highest estate and gift tax rate is 40 percent') and CRS R48183 ('The estate tax rate on the taxable portion of the estate, if any, is 40%'). Prior flag X16 resolved.

rows.label: 2026 long-term capital gain brackets, single: 0% up to $49,450; 15% to $545,500; 20% above
rows.notes: Married filing jointly: 0% to $98,900; 15% to $613,700. Estates/trusts: 0% to $3,300; 15% to $16,250.

rows.label: Basis of inherited property = fair market value at date of death (step-up)
rows.notes: Pub 551 'Basis of Assets' covers basis of property acquired from a decedent; the specific inherited-property text was not read this session (verify on the linked page). Sale soon after death generally produces little or no gain.

rows.label: Net investment income tax thresholds (3.8%)
rows.value: 3.8% on the lesser of net investment income or MAGI over $200,000 (single) / $250,000 (MFJ)
rows.notes: IRS NIIT Q&A: thresholds not indexed for inflation; income includes rental and royalty income and gain on the sale of a second home that is not a principal residence; gain excluded under IRC §121 on a principal residence is not subject. Flag X19 resolved 2026-11-06.

rows.label: Residential rental property depreciation period (GDS)
rows.notes: Used only in the tax discussion; rental income tax not modeled in projections.

rows.label: Assessed value increase cap for property without change in ownership
rows.value: Limited to inflation, not more than 2% per year
rows.notes: Factored base year value; decreases allowed.

rows.label: Prop 19 excluded amount (value cap) for transfers Feb 16, 2025 – Feb 15, 2027
rows.notes: Next adjustment February 2027. Projection assumes future adjustments follow inflation (flagged assumption).

rows.label: Prop 19 New Taxable Value formula (family home, 100% transferred)
rows.value: Factored base year value + (full cash value − excluded amount), i.e., full cash value − $1,044,586 when value exceeds the cap
rows.notes: Excluded amount = factored base year value + $1M cap; excess is added to the base.

rows.label: Prop 19 applies to transfers by reason of death, including distributions from a trust
rows.notes: 'Transfer' includes transfers occurring due to death, whether within or outside a trust.

rows.label: Prop 19 family-home exclusion conditions
rows.value: Heir must occupy as principal residence within 1 year of transfer and claim the Homeowners' Exemption (Form BOE-266) within 1 year; file exclusion claim (Form BOE-19-P) within 3 years
rows.notes: Family home = dwelling eligible for homeowners' or disabled veterans' exemption from the transferor's ownership and occupancy. Rental homes are not eligible. Filing windows per BOE Prop 19 checklist (verified 2026-11-06).

rows.label: Rental property is excluded from the Prop 19 parent-child exclusion
rows.notes: The third unit in Property B would be treated under the family-home definition; mixed-use treatment must be confirmed by the SF Assessor (flagged).

rows.label: Documentary transfer tax, statutory base rate
rows.notes: Counties may impose; the Santa Clara County and San Francisco adopted rates were not confirmed on official pages (flagged).

rows.label: Transfer tax exemption for transfers by reason of death or inter vivos gift, outright or in trust
rows.notes: Claim on the recorded deed; see inheritance process.

rows.label: Preliminary Change of Ownership Report (BOE-502-A) required on transfer
San Francisco secured property tax rate, FY2026-27
rows.notes: Secondary sites listed 1.18268325% for an earlier year; the official figure is used. Supplemental assessments follow a change in ownership.

rows.label: SF secured property tax due dates and penalty
rows.value: 1st installment delinquent after Dec 10 (10%); 2nd after Apr 10 (10% plus fees)

rows.label: SF allowable annual rent increase, covered units, Mar 1, 2026 – Feb 28, 2027
rows.notes: Applies to covered units; not all units are covered. Confirm coverage with the Rent Board.

rows.label: SFPUC W-1B multi-family water: service charge per meter per month (FY2026-27)
rows.notes: Eff. 7/1/2026; adopted Apr 28, 2026 (Res. 26-0064/0066/0068 per schedule).

rows.label: SFPUC W-1B quantity charge per dwelling unit (first 3 units)
rows.notes: Sewer and stormwater charges are not in the excerpt reviewed; cannot reconcile user's total without bills (flagged).

rows.label: San Jose Water Schedule No. 1 (portions of Cupertino): 5/8-inch service charge
rows.notes: Eff. 7/1/2026 (CPUC-approved tariff). Confirm the water provider for the actual service address (not published).

rows.label: San Jose Water residential quantity rates per 100 cu ft (ccf)
rows.notes: At the user's $100–150/month range, implied usage for a 5/8-inch meter is roughly 4–9 ccf/month (computed from the tariff; see flags).

rows.label: PG&E Base Services Charge applies to almost all residential customers (income-graduated daily fixed charge)
rows.notes: Applicability confirmed on the advice-letter status page; the per-day tier amounts ($0.19713 / $0.39688 / $0.79343) were not confirmed on the fetched pages and are flagged.

rows.label: U.S. CPI, 12-month change, September 2026
rows.notes: BLS news release USDL-26-1574 fetched 2026-11-06: CPI-U +3.7% over 12 months; core (less food and energy) +2.6%; electricity +4.4%. Flag X20 resolved.

rows.label: Federal Reserve longer-run inflation objective (PCE)
rows.notes: Base-case inflation assumption.

rows.label: H.R.1301 Death Tax Repeal Act (119th Congress)
rows.value: Introduced Feb 13, 2025; referred to House Ways and Means; no further action recorded
rows.notes: Status as of access; not law.

rows.label: Prop 19 repeal measure on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot
rows.value: Not on the official list of qualified measures
rows.notes: Conflicting secondary blog claims were not used. Official list reviewed: Props 1–5 and 37–45.

rows.label: Prop 43: two-thirds vote for voter-initiated local special taxes (from Jan 1, 2027 if passed)
rows.value: Measure text confirmed; result not certified
rows.notes: Preliminary returns showed the measure trailing (45.2% yes / 54.8% no at 11 p.m. Nov 3). Official certification pending; not a final result.

rows.label: California personal income tax brackets, 2026 (for capital-gain planning)
rows.notes: FTB 2026 California Tax Rate Schedules retrieved 2026-11-06. Flag X17 resolved.

rows.label: California estate or inheritance tax
rows.value: None — California does not conform to the federal estate/GST tax; the state estate 'pick-up' tax equals the repealed federal credit, i.e., $0
rows.notes: FTB: 'Because the federal estate tax credit was repealed, the state's pick-up tax is zero.' No California inheritance tax either. Flag X18 resolved 2026-11-06.

rows.label: Share of U.S. decedents who owe federal estate tax
rows.notes: CRS R48183: declined from 2.1% of the population (2001) to 0.07% (2019). Context for how rarely the tax applies.

rows.label: Combined federal estate & gift basic exclusion for a couple with portability, 2026
rows.value: $30,000,000 ($15M each, including the deceased spouse's unused exclusion)
rows.notes: Portability requires a timely filed Form 706 for the first spouse to die (IRS).

rows.label: AB 1482 statewide rent cap (California Tenant Protection Act)
rows.value: 5% + CPI or 10% max per 12 months (lower of the two), max two increases/year; sunsets Jan 1, 2030
rows.notes: Applies to a Property A rental while the heir lives elsewhere; owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units are exempt. SF covered units also follow SF Rent Board rules.

rows.label: CA SB 284 (2025-26): extend Prop 19 family-home/farm exclusion to eligible transferees
rows.value: Active bill, not law — held in Assembly committee (last action July 14, 2025)
rows.notes: Would change who can use the intergenerational exclusion. Watch status.

rows.label: S.587 Death Tax Repeal Act of 2025 (119th Congress)
rows.value: Introduced Feb 13, 2025; referred to Senate Finance; not law
rows.notes: Would repeal the federal estate and GST taxes. Companion bill H.R. 1301 in the House. Neither enacted as of 2026-11-06.

rows.label: Santa Clara County total property tax rate structure (FY 2025-26)
rows.value: 1.000% base rate + voter-approved debt by Tax Rate Area; example TRA totals 1.12580%–1.24090%
rows.notes: Exact TRA for Property A needs a parcel lookup (kept off-site for privacy). Owner-billed totals imply 1.32%–1.41% — see flags X04/X06.
